1928.text: Select the option having all the correct characteristics.
1928.sol: Options (a), (b), (c) and (d) show neutrophil, basophil, eosinophil and monocyte respectively. Neutrophils are the most abundant cells (60-65 %) of the total WBCs and basophils are the least (0.5 - 1 %) among them. Neutrophils and monocytes (6-8 %) are phagocytic cells. Eosinophils (2 - 3 %) resist infections and are also associated with allergic reactions.

70921.subject: Biology
70921.text: When certain exotic species is introduced accidentally into a new geographic area, then which of the following is more likely to happen?
70921.sol: When an exotic species is introduced accidentally or intentionally into a new geographical area, it often becomes invasive and starts spreading rapidly. This rapid spread is primarily due to the absence of its natural predators in the new environment, which would otherwise keep its population under control. Therefore, the exotic species starts spreading rapidly. Answer: Exotic species start spreading rapidly.

71101.subject: Biology
71101.text: Which of the following epochs marks the major radiation of modern birds?
71101.sol: The question asks for the epoch that marks the major radiation of modern birds. The extinction of non-avian dinosaurs at the end of the Cretaceous period (Mesozoic era) left many ecological niches vacant. In the subsequent Cenozoic era, modern birds (Neornithes) underwent a rapid and massive evolutionary radiation to fill these niches. The Palaeocene epoch (the first epoch of the Cenozoic era) is widely recognized in evolutionary biology and paleontology as the time when the major adaptive radiation of modern birds

71179.subject: Biology
71179.text: The secretion of estrogen is carried out by the ________ under the influence of FSH.
71179.sol: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) stimulates the growth and development of ovarian follicles. As the primary follicle develops into a secondary follicle, it acquires multiple layers of granulosa cells and a new theca layer. The theca interna cells, along with the granulosa cells of the growing secondary follicle, are primarily responsible for the secretion of estrogen under the influence of FSH. Answer: Secondary follicle

71413.subject: Biology

options: Makes cervix hostile to the sperm

71413.sol: Cu-T is a copper-releasing Intra Uterine Device (IUD). The copper ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD. Hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms. Answer: Makes cervix hostile to the sperm

79372.subject: Botany
79372.text: Identify the wrong statement in the context of heartwood.
options: Organic compounds are deposited in it
It conducts water and minerals efficiently
It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls
79372.sol: Heartwood is physiologically inactive due to the deposition of organic compounds and tyloses formation, so this will not conduct water and minerals. Heartwood is the central cylinder found in tree trunks. Heartwood forms as the tree ages, and the inner xylem cells lose the capacity to transmit water. Heartwood tends to be darker in colour than sapwood since it is normally filled with various types of oils, dyes, and sugars. The primary function of heartwood is to provide adequate support to the tree.

79572.subject: Botany
79572.text: Which of the following organisms are known as chief producers in the oceans?
79572.sol: Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans, and they contribute to 40% of the ocean's primary productivity. They constitute a major group of unicellular eukaryotic microscopic algae and are among the most common types of phytoplanktons found floating on the surface of the seas. The other given organisms also exhibit an autotrophic mode of nutrition, however, their productivity is lesser as compared to diatoms.

Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm.
79700.sol: A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but lacks a nucleus. The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the nucleus of companion cells. The enzyme catalyses the interconversion of fumarate and succinate, and is closely related to fumarate reductase. Related Theory The major significance of the citric acid cycle is to act as the final common pathway for the oxidation of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins, since glucose, fatty acids and many amino acids are all metabolised to acetyl CoA.

80533.sol: Commellina benghalensis or kankauoa bears aerial, chasmogamous (stigma and anthers exposed to pollinating agents), insect pollinated flowers and underground cleistogamous flowers. Cleistogamous flowers are bisexual flowers which never open, i.e., always remain closed. In such flowers the anthers and stigma lie very close to each other. 80784.subject: Chemistry
80784.text: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure ?
80784.sol: The primary structure of a protein refers to the linear sequence of amino acids. The secondary structure refers to the local folded structures that form within a polypeptide due to interactions between atoms of the backbone. The most common types of secondary structures are the -helix and the -pleated sheet. The tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional structure of a polypeptide. The quaternary structure is the arrangement of multiple folded protein or coiling protein molecules in a multi-subunit complex

84429.text: What will happen if the stretch receptors of the urinary bladder wall are totally removed?
options: Urine will not collect in the bladder
Urine will continue to collect normally in the bladder
84429.sol: The urinary bladder is a pear shaped, hollow muscular organ situated in the pelvic cavity, which is made up of smooth and involuntary muscles. The lumen of urinary bladder is lined by transition epithelium, which has great power of stretching. If stretch receptors of urinary bladder wall are totally removed, the urine will continue to collect normally in the bladder.

84562.subject: Zoology
84562.text: Cancerous cells can be easily destroyed by radiations due to:
84562.sol: Cancer cells rapidly undergo mitosis. Cancer cells which divide rapidly are less organized than healthy cells. Cancerous cells can easily be destroyed by radiation due to the ability of radiations to kill cells is highest in the tissue with highest number of dividing cells. Hence, tumours are killed more rapidly by radiations.

84613.subject: Zoology
84613.text: Given below are two statements regarding oogenesis. Statement I : The primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells, a theca and shows fluid filled cavity antrum. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the opti
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
84613.sol: Option (4) is the answer because, each primary follicle gets surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca and are called secondary follicles. The secondary follicles soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. The Graafian follicle now ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovum) from the ovary by the process called ovulation. So, the statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.

120839.text: Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R . Assertion A : Amylose is insoluble in water. Reason R : Amylose is a long linear molecule with more than 200 glucose units. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A .

120839.sol: Amylose is a polysaccharide used in various industries as a functional biomaterial. It is mainly a linear component consisting of about 100-10,000 glucose monomers linked by 1,4 alpha bindings. Amylose is a polymer that can be found in starch. It is a water-soluble component that accounts for 20 to 25% of starch. So, among the given two statements first statement is false and second statement is correct.

121341.subject: Botany
121341.text: The spores produced by Phycomycetes are-
options: Exogenous in origin, produced by ascocarp
Endogenous in origin, produced by sporangium
Exogenous in origin, produced by sporangium
Exogenous in origin produced by Basidium
121341.sol: Members of phycomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants. The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in sporangium. A zygospore is formed by fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar in morphology (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous). Some common examples are Mucor, Rhizopus (the breadmould men

121722.subject: Botany
121722.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as

121821.subject: Botany
121821.text: What does the zygote produce in Pteridophytes?
121821.sol: Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes . In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes in these plants are

121994.subject: Botany

121994.sol: Archegonium produces female gametes Antheridium produces male gametes Sporangium is responsible for spore production Ovule develops into a seed after fertilization

122173.subject: Botany
122173.sol: Class Phaeophyceae includes brown algae Brown algae are marine plants. Chief pigments found in the members of this class are chloropyll a and c , -carotene, violaxanthin, fucoxanthin, lutein, diatoxanthin. Reserve food is laminarin, mannitol and oils.

122182.subject: Botany
122182.text: What level of cellular organization is exhibited by coelenterates?
122182.sol: Inspite of differences in structure and form of different animals, there are fundamental features common to various individuals in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems.Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. Some division

122542.subject: Botany
122542.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes a fundamental anatomical difference between Periplaneta (cockroach) and Rana (frog)?
options: Rana possesses a dorsal heart, whereas Periplaneta possesses a ventral heart.
Both Periplaneta and Rana possess a solid, double ventral nerve cord.
Periplaneta possesses a dorsal, hollow nerve cord, whereas Rana possesses a ventral, solid nerve cord.
Periplaneta possesses a dorsal heart, whereas Rana possesses a ventral heart.
122542.sol: Periplaneta (cockroach) belongs to the phylum Arthropoda, which is a non-chordate group. In non-chordates, if a heart is present, it is located dorsally, and the central nervous system is ventral, solid, and double. Rana (frog) belongs to the class Amphibia, which is a chordate group. Chordates are characterized by a ventral heart and a dorsal, hollow, and single central nervous system. Therefore, Periplaneta has a dorsal heart while Rana has a ventral heart. The other options incorrectly assign or swap these funda

122766.subject: Botany
122766.text: What are the two parts of the embryo in a seed?
122766.sol: Above the hilum is a small pore called the micropyle. Within the seed coat is the embryo, consisting of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons . The cotyledons are often fleshy and full of reserve food materials. At the two ends of the embryonal axis are present the radicle and the plumule.

123520.subject: Botany
123520.text: In monocot roots which types of vascular bundles are found?
123520.sol: When xylem and phloem groups are located on different radii, the bundles are said to be radial e.g. root. The protoxylem element lie at the periphery and metaxylem in the centre, this condition is called exarch e.g. root.

124243.subject: Botany
124243.text: Which of the following is correct?
options: Cells of all living organisms have a nucleus
Both animal and plant cells have a well defined cell wall
In prokaryotes, there are no membrane bound organelles
Cells are formed de novo from abiotic materials
124243.sol: In prokaryotes, there are no membrane bound organelles

124577.subject: Botany
124577.text: Which compound was first discovered as a cytokinin?
124577.sol: Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Cytokinins have specific effects on cytokinesis, and were discovered as kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

124737.subject: Botany
124737.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Application of cytokinins helps in retaining the green colour of leaves for a longer period. Reason (R): Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
124737.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because cytokinins delay the process of leaf senescence, thereby keeping the leaves green for a longer duration. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the physiological basis for this effect. According to NCERT, cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence. Thus, the nutrient mobilisation is the direct cause of the delayed senescence. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Answer: Both (A) and (R) are corr

125052.sol: Statements a and d are correct

125350.subject: Botany
125350.text: What is the relationship between the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a and the rate of photosynthesis?
125350.sol: The wavelengths at which there is maximum absorption by chlorophyll a, i.e., in the blue and the red regions, also indicates direct relation to higher rate of photosynthesis . Hence, we can conclude that chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis. Though chlorophyll is the major pigment responsible for trapping light, other thylakoid pigments like chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids, which are called accessory pigments, also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a. Indee

125479.subject: Botany
125479.text: At what CO2 concentration do C4 plants show saturation?
125479.sol: Carbon dioxide is the major limiting factor for photosynthesis. The concentration of CO2 is very low in the atmosphere (between 0.03 and 0.04 per cent). Increase in concentration upto 0.05 per cent can cause an increase in CO2 fixation rates; beyond this the levels can become damaging over longer periods. The C3 and C4 plants respond differently to CO2 concentrations. At low light conditions neither group responds to high CO2 conditions. At high light intensities, both C3 and C4 plants show increase in the rates of

126183.subject: Botany
126183.text: What is the difference between hypocotyl and epicotyl?
options: the region of embryo above the cotyledon is hypocotyl while the region of embryo below the cotyledon is epicot
the region of embryo below the cotyledon is hypocotyl while the region of embryo above the cotyledon is epicot
hypocotyl terminates at the cotyledonary node while the epicotyl terminates at the plumule
126183.sol: The difference between hypocotyl and epicotyl is the region of embryo above the cotyledon is hypocotyl while the region of embryo below the cotyledon is epicotyl

Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126607.sol: A number of enzymes require metal ions for their activity which form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate. For example, zinc is a cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.

127063.subject: Botany
127063.text: Assertion : Dimethyl mercury is a highly persistent pollutant that accumulates in food chains. Reason : Mercury pollution is responsible for minamata.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
127063.sol: Mercury is an important toxic pollutant. It is changed to water soluble dimethyl mercury which undergoes biomagnification, i.e., accumulates in the body of organisms inhabiting in the water. Eating poisoned animals causes deformity known as minamata disease which is characterized by diarrhoea, impairment of various senses, numbness of lips, blurring of vision, mental dearrangement and death.

127277.subject: Botany
127277.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: There are probably more than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species yet to be discovered and described. Reason: Only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127277.sol: If we accept May’s global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. Applying this proportion to India’s diversity figures, we estimate that there are probably more than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species yet to be discovered and described.

127447.subject: Botany
127447.text: Which of the following is not a method of ex situ conservation?
127447.sol: Ex-situ conservation is off-site conservation in which the animals are conserved in a protected environment under special care. It is conservation of selected rare plants/animals in places outside their natural homes. Ex-situ conservation includes offsite botanical gardens, zoo, seed banks, micropropagation, cryopreservation, In vitro fertilization, etc. An area where animal habitats and their surroundings are protected from any sort of disturbance is known as in situ conservation, National parks are examples of th

127483.subject: Botany
127483.text: Select the correct statement about biodiversity
options: The desert areas of Rajasthan and Gujarat have a very high level of desert animal species as well as numerous
Large scale planting of Bt cotton has no adverse effect on biodiversity
Western Ghats have a very high degree of species richness and endemism
Conservation of biodiversity is just a fad pursued by the developed countries
127483.sol: Western Ghat occur along the Western Coast of India in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. There is high degree of endemism as well as richness of species of flowering plants, amphibians reptiles, some mammals and butterflies. B t cotton is insect resistant and thus disturbed the food chain.

127826.subject: Botany
127826.text: Read the following paragraph and identify the correct sequence of terms for the blanks [A], [B], and [C]. [A] - Net primary productivity, [B] - Secondary productivity, [C] - Gross primary productivity

127826.sol: Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. Thus, [A] is Gross primary productivity. Net primary productivity (NPP) is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers), which remains after plant respiration. Thus, [B] is Net primary productivity. Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Thus, [C] is Secondary productivity. Answer: [A] - Gross primary productivity, [B] -

127885.subject: Zoology
127885.text: Which organ consists of all four types of tissues?
127885.sol: Explanation. The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. We also notice, after some careful

128703.subject: Zoology
128703.text: Assertion : Small intestine is the principal organ for absorption of nutrients. Reason : Absorption of water, simple sugars and alcohol etc. takes place in small intestine.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
128703.sol: Absorption of substances takes place in different parts of the alimentary canal, like mouth, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. However, maximum absorption occurs in the small intestine. Hence, small intestine is the principal organ for absorption of nutrients. The digestion is completed here and the final products of digestion such as glucose, fructose, fatty acids, glycerol and amino acids are absorbed through the mucosa into the blood stream and lymph. Absorption of water, single sugars and alcohol, e

129035.subject: Zoology
129035.text: A patient's blood report indicates an absolute basophil count of 40 - 80 cells/cu.mm. Assuming this represents the normal healthy percentage range for basophils, what would be the expected absolute number of neutrophils in the same volume of blood?
129035.sol: According to NCERT, basophils constitute 0.5 - 1 % of the total WBCs. Given the absolute basophil count is 40 - 80 cells/cu.mm, we can determine the total WBC count. If 0.5 - 1 % corresponds to 40 - 80 cells, then 1 % corresponds to 80 cells. Total WBC count = 80 100 = 8000 cells/cu.mm. Neutrophils constitute 60 - 65 % of the total WBCs. Expected number of neutrophils = 60 100 8000 to 65 100 8000 = 4800 - 5200 cells/cu.mm. Calculating the lymphocyte count ( 20 - 25 % ) would yield 1600 - 2000 cells/cu.mm, which is

129182.subject: Zoology
129182.text: What are the two parts of the human neural system?
options: Central neural system and peripheral neural system
129182.sol: The human neural system is divided into two parts: the central neural system (CNS) and the peripheral neural system (PNS). The CNS includes the brain and spinal cord and is the site of information processing and control. The afferent nerve fibres transmit impulses from tissues/organs to the CNS. The efferent nerve fibres transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues/organs.The somatic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to skeletal muscles. The autonomic neural system transmit

129571.subject: Zoology
129571.text: Which organ is the largest gland in the human body?
129571.sol: Other than the kidneys, lungs, liver and skin also help in the elimination of excretory wastes. Our lungs remove large amounts of CO2 (approximately 200mL/minute) and also significant quantities of water every day. Liver, the largest gland in our body , secretes bile-containing substances like bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs.Most of these substances ultimately pass out alongwith digestive wastes.

129796.subject: Zoology
129796.text: Which pleural membrane is in close contact with the thoracic lining?
options: Both inner and outer pleural membranes are in close contact with the thoracic lining
Neither inner nor outer pleural membrane is in close contact with the thoracic lining
129796.sol: The outer pleural membrane is in close contact with the thoracic lining. whereas the inner pleural membrane is in contact with the lung surface. The part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitute the conducting part whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Exchange p

130702.sol: Sterilisation procedure in the male is called ‘vasectomy. In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.

The result was that 15N was incorporated into newly synthesized DNA (as well as other nitrogen containing compounds). This heavy DNA molecule could be distinguished from the normal DNA by centrifugation in a cesium chloride (CsCl) density gradient (Please note that 15N is not a radioactive isotope, and it can be separated from 14N only based on densities). (ii) Then they tran

131590.subject: Zoology
131590.text: What is the inducer for the lac operon?
131590.sol: Lactose is the substrate for the enzyme beta-galactosidase and it regulates switching on and off of the operon. Hence, it is termed as inducer. In the absence of a preferred carbon source such as glucose, if lactose is provided in the growth medium of the bacteria, the lactose is transported into the cells through the action of permease (Remember, a very low level of expression of lac operon has to be present in the cell all the time, otherwise lactose cannot enter the cells). The lactose then induces the operon in

131915.subject: Zoology
131915.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): During transcription, the opening of the DNA double helix requires the enzyme DNA helicase. Reason (R): DNA-dependent RNA polymerase inherently facilitates the opening of the DNA helix during the process of transcription. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the opti
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
131915.sol: Assertion (A) is false because a separate DNA helicase enzyme is not required to unwind the DNA double helix during transcription. DNA helicase is primarily involved in unwinding the helix during DNA replication. Reason (R) is true because the enzyme DNA-dependent RNA polymerase itself facilitates the opening of the DNA helix and continues elongation during transcription. Therefore, (A) is false but (R) is true. Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

132083.subject: Zoology
132083.text: Which factor is dominant in the context of tall and dwarf traits?
132083.sol: As Mendel found the phenotype of the F1 heterozygote Tt to be exactly like the TT parent in appearance, he proposed that in a pair of dissimilar factors, one dominates the other (as in the F1 ) and hence is called the dominant factor while the other factor is recessive . In this case T (for tallness) is dominant over t (for dwarfness), that is recessive. He observed identical behaviour for all the other characters/trait-pairs that he studied.

132697.subject: Zoology
132697.text: What was the explanation for the increase in dark-winged moths after industrialization?
options: Dark-winged moths were better adapted to warmer climates
White-winged moths could camouflage better in the dark environment
Predators were better able to spot white-winged moths against dark backgrounds
Dark-winged moths had a higher reproductive rate
132697.sol: The increase in dark-winged moths was explained by predators being better able to spot white-winged moths against the darkened tree trunks, leading to higher survival rates for the dark-winged moths .During post- industrialisation period, the tree trunks became dark due to industrial smoke and soots. Under this condition the white-winged moth did not survive due to predators, dark-winged or melanised moth survived. Before industrialisation set in, thick growth of almost white-coloured lichen covered the trees - in

133064.subject: Zoology
133064.sol: Humans, or human beings, are bipedal primates belonging to the mammalian species Homo sapiens (Latin "wise man" or "knowing man") in the family Hominidae (the great apes). It includes both archaric and modern humans, as well as the subspecies Homo sapeins neanderthalensis, also known as the Neanderthals. Homo sapiens first started appearing about 500,000 or fewer years ago.

133616.subject: Zoology
133616.text: Assertion : Interferons are antiviral proteins. Reason : Interferons are secreted by virus infected cells.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
133616.sol: Virus infected cells secrete proteins known as interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection. In humans three groups of interferons have been discovered : (1) - interferons (2) - interferons (3) - interferons

133645.subject: Zoology
133645.text: Assertion : Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) originated in China. Reason : China is the most populated country of the world.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false
if both Assertion and Reason are false statements
133645.sol: SARS, a severe acute type of 'Atypically atypical pneumonia' caused by metapneumo virus (a type of corona virus) was first reported (WHO) in China (Beijing, Guangdong, HongKong, Taiwan etc.) Though China is the most populated country of the world, it is not directly responsible for the origin of SARS. The killer pneumonia virus is responsible for SARS origin.

134073.text: What is the role of biotechnology in agriculture?

Biotechnology is used to produce biogas from plant waste.
Biotechnology is used to treat sewage through the process of activated sludge formation.
Biotechnology is used to purify proteins and organic compounds.
134073.sol: Biotechnology has an application in agriculture through the creation of genetically modified crops for agriculture. 134865.sol: During the isolation of genetic material, the cells must be broken open to release DNA along with other macromolecules. 6a1bb6bf107bf677676d9f7f.sol: Sugarcane, Maize, and Sorghum are C₄ plants, whereas Tomato is a C₃ plant. C₄ plants show saturation in the rate of photosynthesis at about 360 L L ⁻¹ of CO ₂ . Therefore, increasing the CO ₂ concentration from 380 L L ⁻¹ to 430 L L ⁻¹ will not increase their photosynthetic rate, as they are already saturated. C₃ plants respond to increased CO ₂ concentration and show saturation only beyond 450 L L ⁻¹ . 6a0e277b165ae1327797b414.text: Which of the following microbes is commercially exploited for the production of blood-cholesterol lowering agents?
6a0e277b165ae1327797b414.sol: Statins are widely used as blood-cholesterol lowering agents. They are produced commercially by the yeast Monascus purpureus . 97629.text: The chemiosmotic hypothesis suggests that the ATP are produced on the inner membrane of mitochondria due to:
options: F 1 particles present between the inner and outer membrane of mitochondria.
Involvement of oxygen as the electron acceptor.
Creation of a proton electrochemical gradient across inner membrane of mitochondria.
Enzymes present in the mitochondrial matrix.
97629.sol: The chemiosmotic hypothesis put forth by Sir Peter Mitchell suggests that the proton gradient created across the inner membrane of mitochondria is responsible for the pumping of H + ions into the mitochondrial matrix. This energy produced by the proton pump is harnessed by the catalytic subunit of ATPase enzyme complex to produce ATP. A similar mechanism is seen in the thylakoid membrane of chloroplast during energy production in the light reaction of photosynthesis.

304964.text: Which of the following methods can be utilized to measure the speed of light inside a laboratory?
304964.sol: Foucault's method uses a rotating mirror and a fixed concave mirror separated by a relatively small distance of a few meters. This compact setup allows the experiment to be performed inside a laboratory. Fizeau's method requires a large distance of several kilometers between the source and the mirror. Michelson's method uses a rotating octagonal mirror and requires a very large distance of tens of kilometers. Roemer's method is an astronomical method based on the observation of the eclipses of Jupiter's moons.

306641.text: An experimenter measures the length of a rod. In the scenarios provided, all motions are relative to the lab and parallel to the rod's length. In which scenario will the measured length be minimum?

306619.subject: Physics
306619.text: For a neutral carbon atom in its ground state, the mass is
options: dependent on the form of carbon, such as graphite or charcoal
306619.sol: The unified atomic mass unit ( 1 u ) is defined as exactly 1 12 of the mass of an unbound, neutral carbon-12 atom in its nuclear and electronic ground state. Therefore, the mass of a standard neutral carbon atom (carbon-12) in its ground state is exactly 12 u . The mass of an individual atom is an intrinsic property and does not depend on the macroscopic allotropic form (such as graphite, diamond, or charcoal) it may be a part of.
